pull_request.title: Muon System: establish reach and field benchmarks for magnetic design
pull_request.head: codex/muon-reach-field-study
pull_request.body:
## Executive summary

Establish quantitative muon reach and spectrometer field benchmarks for the next magnetic-system design. The study combines LAYOUT-001, its 3 T tracker field and pinned unmerged HCAL inputs with ATLAS MDT precision assumptions. It includes the requested 3 m span / 500 GeV compact-system comparison and supplies inputs to subsequent design; magnet topology and station construction remain open.

## Change

- Retain reproducible IdRes tracker covariance estimates, finite HCAL material rays, PDG mean-loss transport, field/sagitta calculations, source provenance and plots in `docs/validation/MUON-001/`.
- Use ATLAS 81.7 μm per tube, 35 μm fitted-chamber precision and a separate 30 μm alignment benchmark. Assuming independent station alignment gives 46.1 μm effective coordinates.
- For the central barrel, identify 5 GeV as a candidate lower reconstruction working point and 10 GeV for easier matching. These are analytical working points, not measured efficiencies.
- For a 5 m station span at local 100 GeV, 1% measurement-plus-alignment needs about 0.60 T; including the illustrative uniform 1.3 X₀ internal material gives about 1.35 T. The measurement/scattering crossover is about 200 GeV and is independent of field.
- Address the compact-span review: the tracker proxy gives 6.75% at 500 GeV, so 10% combined alone imposes no minimum muon field. An additional 10% standalone target over 3 m needs about 0.86 T with the assumed internal 1.3 X₀; 1 T gives 8.61% standalone and 5.31% in an ideal independent combination. About 1.4 T preserves the earlier 0.5 T / 5 m intrinsic measurement term.
- Distinguish upstream calorimeter scattering from material within the standalone spectrometer fit. Add a magnetic-design handoff covering station spacing, vector bending, field/energy sizing and remaining validation under DES004.

Inputs include open PRs #64, #70, #71, #81, #84 and #85 at the exact revisions recorded in the report. This PR integrates the study and its evidence; no prototype detector geometry is merged or selected. Tracker material and solenoid composition remain explicit proxies. Full transport, straggling, pattern recognition and reconstruction efficiency remain untested.

## Dashboard and validation

- [x] Updated `project/tracking.json` with MUON-001 evidence and the magnetic-design next action.
- [x] Independent PhysVal/SoftEng replay: 72 IdRes cases agree with retained results and independent GLS; three HCAL rays, four native-module comparisons and five primitive controls reproduce.
- [x] Independent compact-span review: 48 additional IdRes cases and all 12 overlapping 100 GeV controls reproduce; span scaling, target roots and combination controls pass. The code rejects unsupported high-energy stopping-power extrapolation.
- [x] Mean transport convergence, high-momentum Highland limit and field-scaling controls pass; numerical controls added to CI.
- [x] Session journal validation, project-record validation and layout drawing check pass. Post-merge unit suites: 33 session-log tests and 28 project-record tests pass.
- [x] Preserved human-only sign-off boundaries and prior 180 μm evidence.
- [x] Layout geometry and R–Z drawing are unchanged; the candidate page links the new design input.

comments.body:
Here's a question to get this further:
- the attempt is to make the muon system a bit less spacious: potentially, ideally from 5m chamber span to 3m
- the tracker + 3T solenoid gives roughly 1% at 100 GeV resolution, from the presented study a 0.5 T magnetic field at a 5m span does a similar trick for the muon system
- let's assume that we want a combined muon resolution of 10 % at 0.5 TeV would that be feasible and what magnetic strength would we need given your X0 estimate ?

Addressed in 679774e with the [compact-span calculation, plots and retained IdRes evidence](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/679774e16b94e211652358e59dd67bcb634745ba/docs/validation/MUON-001/compact-span/results.md).

Yes, a **3 m span is feasible within this covariance estimate**. The rerun central 3 T tracker proxy gives **6.75% at 500 GeV**, so the requested **10% combined target alone does not impose a positive minimum muon field**. A useful additional criterion is 10% standalone muon precision: that requires **about 0.86 T over 3 m**, with the existing 46.1 μm effective station uncertainty and assumed uniform internal 1.3 X₀.

At a common 500 GeV reference:

| Span | Average bending field | Standalone muon | Ideal tracker + muon |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 m | 0.5 T | 6.49% | 4.68% |
| 3 m | 0.5 T | 17.22% | 6.28% |
| 3 m | 1.0 T | 8.61% | 5.31% |
| 3 m | 1.4 T | 6.15% | 4.55% |

For preserving the earlier 0.5 T / 5 m intrinsic measurement term, the field scales as `B L²`: **0.5 × (5/3)² = 1.39 T**. I suggest comparing **1 T** and **1.4 T** compact candidates in the magnetic design. At 100 GeV, the earlier 0.5 T / 5 m muon estimate was 1.21% for measurement/alignment and 2.70% including the assumed internal scattering.

The material distinction matters: **1.3 X₀ is the internal spectrometer benchmark**, whereas the roughly **106 X₀ calorimeter/solenoid budget is upstream**, affecting matching and constrained fits. The report includes internal-material sensitivity (a 10% standalone target needs 0.93 T for 5 X₀ or 1.03 T for 10 X₀). Combined numbers are ideal independent-curvature comparisons; they omit energy-loss straggling and shared covariances. No 500 GeV transport is extrapolated from the existing ≤100 GeV stopping-power tables.

Validation: 48 new IdRes cases reproduce an independent execution, all 12 overlapping 100 GeV controls agree, and the compact-span formulas/roots passed separate physics review. Numerical controls and 33 session/document-link tests pass; GitHub CI is running for this update.
